analysis: Performance has saturated. Every top recipe scores between 0.992 and 1.0, and one build out of 512 is worth 0.002. The binomial standard error near p=0.996 is about 0.003, so these recipes cannot be told apart reliably. Average dev success by recipe: depth-2 layernorm with 64 envs gives 0.998 (2 seeds); depth-3 layernorm with 128 envs gives 0.997 (4 seeds); gamma 0.99 gives 0.996 (4 seeds), so it adds nothing. Without layernorm, depth-2 gives 0.994. The cheap t15 recipe (about 200s) is the strongest candidate for selection. The remaining budget should check that it holds up across seeds and try a few low-risk changes that might fix the last few failed builds: a higher learning rate, a wider network, and lower entropy for greedy evaluation.

proposals.hypothesis: Noise test: an exact repeat of t15/t16 (depth-2 layernorm, 64 envs, iou_delta) with a third seed. This checks that the leading cheap recipe stays at or above 0.996 before final selection. Refuted (not robust) if dev success is below 0.994.

Change: t15 with lr 0.002. Raising lr from 5e-4 to 1e-3 was a large gain, layernorm should keep a higher rate stable, and linear decay anneals it late in training. Refuted if dev success is below 0.996 or train success drops below 0.985.

Change: t15 with width 64→128. More channels per cell may fix the rare overhang and build-order cases at the same depth. My runtime estimate is about 350–450s. Refuted if dev success is below 0.996 or the run exceeds 600s.

Change: t15 with ent_coef 0.01→0.003. Evaluation is greedy and train success is about 0.987, so a sharper policy may convert the remaining near-misses. On depth 3 (t13) this matched the best result without hurting. Refuted if dev success is below 0.996.
